Date: 2026-10-22
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (SummitHealth Head of ML), Evan Garcia (Engineering Manager), Sara Lee (Security Architect)
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked SummitHealth through the Model Catalog UI, selection criteria for open models, and benchmark/compatibility matrices. Customer is evaluating hosted vs Dedicated and private deployment for PHI-sensitive workloads. Key asks: run benchmark with SummitHealth prompts, confirm quantization/hardware compatibility, and share pricing + pilot options.
topics: Compatibility matrix (quantization, GPU types, sequence lengths)
Deployment options: hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
Next steps: benchmarks, pricing, POC scoping
transcript: 00:00 Speaker 1 (Ava): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we appreciate the time. Today Liam and I will run through the model catalog and how you'd pick open models for different workloads.

00:18 Priya: Thanks, Ava. Quick context: we're looking at a mix of triage chatbots and document summarization for patient notes. Latency SLOs are around 300ms for quick replies, and cost is a big factor.

00:36 Liam: Yep, got it. We'll show the catalog filters, the perf profiles and then a compatibility matrix that maps quantization to GPU families. Also we'll call out where KV cache and prefix caching helps.
00:55 Evan: And from infra side, we need to know what GPUs you support if we go Dedicated or Private — A100, H100, and anything on-prem compatible would be good to confirm.
01:12 Sara: Also security — SOC2, SSO, KMS and audit logs. We may need private deployment for PHI. We'll ask specific questions there.

01:36 Liam: Totally. Quick demo then: opening the model catalog — you'll see default filters like task (chat, completion, embeddings), license (open, commercial), size, and throughput profile. For open models we tag quantization-ready variants and we show measured per-token latency on an A100 and on H100.
01:56 (audio glitch) 02:01 Speaker 2 (Priya): Could you show an example for a 7B vs 13B model tradeoff?

02:15 Liam: Sure — here's a 7B open model we recommend for low-latency chat. The benchmark card shows median latency 120ms on A100 with int8, throughput of ~85 tokens/sec in our standard batching. For the 13B, latency goes up to ~220ms but quality improves on long-form summarization.
02:42 Priya: Are those numbers from your public bench or internal runs? We need to run our prompts too — shape matters.

02:55 Ava: Great point. We have a benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/summithealth) — we'll populate it with your prompts and token distributions. That gives realistic numbers for your workloads.

03:13 Evan: Nice. Also compatibility matrix — does Redwood support quantization formats like int8, nf4, and do those work across H100 and A100? We've heard sometimes int8 on older kernels has instability.

03:30 Liam: We surface a compatibility matrix per model version: whether int8/nf4/4bit are supported, and recommended kernels. There are a few known caveats — e.g., some int8 kernels need specific CUDA driver versions. We'll flag those in the matrix.
03:48 Sara: For Private deployment, how much of that matrix is enforced vs opt-in? We can't risk an unsupported quantization in a production cluster.

04:02 Liam: For Private, you control the runtime config; we recommend profiles. The console can apply a validation check before rollout and will block incompatible quantization/compile steps. If you want, we can include a preflight check in the POC.
04:20 Priya: That'd be useful. Regarding cost, how does Redwood compare with running vanilla self-hosted on preemptible GPUs? We're optimizing $/token as well.

04:33 Ava: We typically show $/token for hosted, and a separate estimate for Dedicated. Our Optimize toolkit will recommend batching and cache settings to reduce costs — those generate expected savings in the benchmark sheet.
04:51 Evan: Any example of savings? Like 30-40%?

05:00 Liam: Yes. In customer scenarios similar to yours, combining KV cache with a 50ms batching window and int8 quantization reduced token cost by ~35% while keeping p95 latency within SLOs. We'll show a case study later in the deck.
05:18 (brief cross-talk) Speaker 3 (Sara): Sorry, can you repeat KV cache explanation? I heard K-V cash earlier, lol.

05:27 Liam: Ha, K-V cash. It's KV cache — we cache key/value pairs for prior tokens per session to avoid recomputing past context. This gives big wins for multi-turn chat and reduces compute per token.
05:45 Priya: Does caching affect privacy? We need controls for retention and purging per company policy.
05:54 Ava: Yes, retention policies are configurable. For hosted we retain caches transiently; for Private you control retention and purging. We can also encrypt cache using customer KMS keys.
06:10 Evan: Back to model selection: in the UI you had a quality score — what's the basis for that?

06:22 Liam: The quality score aggregates evals across benchmark suites: next-token accuracy, summarization ROUGE, and chat coherency tests. We run open-source evals and include customer-provided eval sets for better alignment.
06:39 Priya: Can we plug our own evals? We want a regression test suite to run on every model upgrade.
06:47 Ava: Absolutely. The Console supports uploading eval sets and will run model regressions on new versions and alert if quality drops. We'll include instructions in the security pack.

07:02 (30s pause) 07:32 Liam: Showing the compatibility matrix — here you can filter by hardware family; for example, H100 has better perf for fp16 kernels on larger models, A100 is still great for int8 on 7B variants.
07:50 Priya: How do you handle mixed workloads? We have some heavy document summarization (long context) and short chat. Do you recommend separate routes?
08:06 Liam: Yes, route by policy: short chat to a fast 7B quantized route, long docs to a 13B fp16 route. Our routing supports automatic fallback if the primary route is overloaded.
08:22 Evan: Is routing at the request level or session level? We have session affinity needs.
08:30 Liam: Request-level with session affinity options. You can pin sessions to a model variant to keep KV cache warm.
08:43 Priya: Can Redwood do A/B tests across models? We want to compare quality between two open models.
08:50 Ava: Yes, rollouts in Console support canary, A/B, and automatic rollback based on quality or latency regressions. You can tie regressions to uploaded eval sets.
09:05 Sara: Security question — audit logs for inference requests? We need full traceability for PHI access.
09:15 Ava: We provide request-level audit logs with redaction options. For Private, logs can be shipped to your SIEM and encrypted with your KMS.
09:30 Evan: About benchmarking with our prompts — what's the typical turnaround?
09:37 Liam: If you send prompts and traffic profile, we can run an initial benchmark in 3–5 business days and populate the sheet. For deeper POC runs with your infra we may need a week.
09:51 Priya: Good. We'll share prompts. Also curious about tokenization differences across models — we saw variance affecting cost.
10:03 Liam: Yep, tokenization matters. The catalog shows tokens-per-word estimates per model family. We can compute exact token counts when you give representative text.

10:20 Ava: Quick pause — shared artifacts: deck (https://redwood.ai/decks/model-catalog-demo), benchmarks sheet (https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/summithealth). We'll attach security docs after this call.
10:33 (minor background noise) 10:40 Priya: One more thing: private deployment — if we go on-prem, what's the upgrade path for model versions? We want controlled rollouts.

10:52 Liam: For Private, we provide a control plane that you host in a VPC. Upgrades are controlled; you can schedule image/weights updates and run dry-run validations with your evals before promoting.
11:09 Evan: Are there requirements on network egress for hosted vs private? Sara, you probably want no egress for PHI.
11:18 Sara: Yes, zero-eDgress if possible. Can Redwood run fully air-gapped?
11:26 Ava: We have an on-prem package that can be air-gapped; there are a few manual steps for weight provisioning and KMS integration. We'll share the checklist.
11:38 Priya: Cost model for Dedicated — do we get committed throughput and burst?
11:45 Ava: Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools with configurable autoscaling and burst capacity. Pricing depends on commit size and SLA tier. We'll include a pricing sheet in the follow-up.

12:00 Liam: Demo closing — showing how to filter catalog for open-license models, then export a compatibility CSV. You can see columns for recommended quantization, tested CUDA drivers, and measured median latency on A100/H100.
12:22 Evan: That CSV export will be useful. Can it include our custom eval columns?
12:29 Liam: Yes, once you upload evals, the export includes your eval metrics per model/version.
12:40 Priya: Great. Any gotchas? We heard some models have tokenization drift between releases.
12:48 Liam: We track tokenizer changes in model metadata and flag breaking changes. Console can block an upgrade if tokenizer drift affects metrics.

13:02 (longer pause) 13:35 Ava: Okay, recap of next steps: we'll populate the benchmarks sheet with your prompts, run an initial perf run, share pricing and Dedicated options, and schedule a POC scoping call for early Nov. Action items in the sheet.
13:50 Priya: Sounds good. Thanks both — excited to see the numbers.
13:57 Sara: Thanks — please include the security checklist for Private deployment.
14:05 Ava: Will do, thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with artifacts and proposed POC dates. Bye.
14:12 (call ends)
